.mib

The .mib (Mix Information Bank) format dictates audio routing, ducking, and DSP states for EA's sound engine in The Simpsons Game (2007). These binary configuration files apply mixing rules to specific audio channels or buses based on active game states (e.g., ducking SFX when dialog plays, or applying EQ for the "Robobart" and "Helium" voice modifiers).

Format Architecture

The PS3 variation of these files uses standard IEEE 754 Big-Endian byte order. The architecture is chunk-based, consisting of a global header followed by sequential, fixed-length parameter blocks representing individual mix nodes.

Offset Type Description Example Value
0x00 byte[32] File magic, versioning, and internal padding. ... 18 ... 0E ...
0x20 uint32 Total Record Count. The number of mix blocks in the file. 0x37 (55 records)
0x24 uint32 Header padding or master file offset. 0x18
0x28 uint32 Global state flags or secondary counts. 0x00000000
0x2C uint32 Master File Hash / ID. 0x0000098C

Mix Record Block (Starts at 0x30)

Each mix target block in standard ducking files is typically 44 bytes (0x2C) long.

  • uint32 Target Hash (4 bytes): An identifier (likely FNVA or EA's custom hash) corresponding to a named audio bus (e.g., 1F 96 D6 52).
  • float32 DSP Parameters (32 bytes): An array of 8 sequential floating-point values determining gain, ducking depth, and fade interpolation.
    • 3F 80 00 00 translates to 1.0 (Unity gain / no attenuation).
    • BF 80 00 00 translates to -1.0 (Often used as a null state or full mute/phase invert).
    • 3F 4C CC CD translates to 0.8 (80% volume ducking).
  • uint32 Block Delimiter/Type (4 bytes): Frequently 00 01 77 00, indicating the end of a parameter array or a specific chunk type identifier.
  • uint32 Block Size (4 bytes): Dictates the size of the next nested array or sibling block (e.g., 00 00 00 2C for 44 bytes).

Implementation Approach

When building a custom parser for the RemakeEngine in Deno, the native DataView API handles the endianness inherently by passing false to the getter methods.

export function parseMibBank(buffer: ArrayBuffer) {
    const view = new DataView(buffer);
    const recordCount = view.getUint32(0x20, false);
    
    let offset = 0x30;
    const mixNodes = [];

    for (let i = 0; i < recordCount; i++) {
        const hash = view.getUint32(offset, false).toString(16);
        const params = [];
        
        for (let p = 0; p < 8; p++) {
            params.push(view.getFloat32(offset + 4 + (p * 4), false));
        }

        const delimiter = view.getUint32(offset + 36, false);
        const nextSize = view.getUint32(offset + 40, false);

        mixNodes.push({ hash, params });
        offset += nextSize > 0 ? nextSize : 44; 
    }
    
    return mixNodes;
}

Files with complex recursive states like the helium modifiers (mix_simpsons1_helium_off.mib) contain shorter header structures (e.g., 0x01 records reported, but variable 0x44 block sizes followed by subsequent appended hash arrays). The nextSize parameter dictates how far the cursor should jump to ingest the proceeding DSP node.
